newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European bourses break records, boosted by US.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European bourses break records, boosted by US.

text.p: European bourses surged on Thursday, many hitting new records, pumped up by a strong overnight rally on Wall Street which put on a whopping 93 points -- more than erasing its losses of the previous day.

London, Frankfurt and Paris were all trading well into record territory and leading shares in many other European centres saw their indexes scale new peaks. On the currency front, the dollar continued to defy gravity, quickly shrugging off a slightly stronger-than expected German employment report and rallying again to set a fresh 34-month peak at 1.7198 marks.
Cause of the bourse bonhomie were the latest comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, whose utterances and nuances are meticulously analysed for clues to credit policy.

Having earlier plunged equity markets into despair with perceived warnings that stocks are overvalued and due for a fall, Greenspan on Wednesday reversed some of the damage in statements to a congressional committee.

Instead of repeating last week's comment that Wall Street's ascent "raised questions of sustainability", he said he did not believe in using monetary policy as a tool to influence share prices. This was interpreted as indicating the Fed would not hike rates simply to lasso the Wall Street bull.
The Dow powered ahead on his comments, ending 93.13 points higher at 6,946.

By 1045 GMT London was up well over half a percent, Frankfurt was up 1.7 percent and the Paris bourse was up 1.2 percent, all at new record index highs, also powered by soaring company profits and a strong dollar.

"We've really gone roaring up," one London dealer said. "Wall Street was good, the results have been good, it's shaping up to be a cracking day. The only problem would be if the early mark-up keeps buyers away."

As the London market opened, pharmaceuticals giant Glaxo Wellcome Plc was the only stock in the FTSE 100 to head downwards, losing ground after annual profits in line with expectations and a cautious outlook for the next two years.
Industrial conglomerate BTR Plc was among the best-performing blue-chips after announcing annual profits which fell short of the previous year but were higher than analysts had forecast.

In Frankfurt, German shares pared some gains in early bourse trade after setting new record high in IBIS DAX electronic dealings. Traders saw the bourse maintaining gains and taking cue for further advances from U.S. market. Dollar strength, at nearly 1.72 marks, is positive for German exports and was helping to underpin shares.

And in Paris, France's CAC-40 index of leading shares was also in record territory. Dealers said the bullish trend was supported by strong liquidity and favourable corporate results. "This sharp rise is certainly due to Wall Street and the dollar but also to Mr. Greenspan who reassured markets," said one dealer.
But shares in carmaker Renault tumbled a further 5.77 percent as fallout continued from planned layoffs in Belgium and France.
A main forcus on the currency markets was German unemployment. The adjusted total was in line with the 4.672 million leaked by German labour market sources on Wednesday.

Analysts said that while the mark may glean some support from the fact the rise in jobless was not as bad as some recent newspaper speculation, the unemployment trend remained gloomy in contrast with the U.S. labour market.
The U.S. February employment report is scheduled for release on Friday and analysts polled by Reuters expect a 230,000 rise in non-farm payrolls during the month.
At 0945 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.7182 marks, up more than half a pfennig from Wednesday's close here at 1.7128.
Meanwhile gold was at lower levels as the market took stock after a scare caused by news that the Swiss central bank would sell reserves to set up a memorial fund.
Switzerland on Wednesday outlined a plan to use official gold reserves to create a humanitarian fund for victims of the Holocaust which would entail selling gold over a 10-year period.
Gold slid in reaction to the prospect of central bank gold reserve sales.
"If one bank uses reserves for this reason there are plenty of opportunities for central banks all over the world of doing something like this," one analyst said.
Gold fixed in London at at $352.15, down from $354.50 on Wednesday afternoon.
CURRENCIES AT 1045 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7182 marks and 121.45 yen, compared with 1.7128 and 121.56 late on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1045 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 26.6 points at 4,386.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 gained 36.86 to 2,703.05
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 49.25 at 3414.24
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $352.15, down from its London close on Wednesday of 352.65.
